component_evaluated: All Models (Flood, Damage, Anomaly, Incident, YOLO)
details: Sensor Anomaly model used 100% REAL data (1,564 clean records from NOAA IBTrACS & IMD). Flood Risk and Damage models used in-memory tables compiled from real station returns and historical assessments, with derived risk labels. Incident text used 30 representative distress messages (derived/semi-synthetic). YOLO correctly flagged UNAVAILABLE without fabricating fake annotations.

Flood risk labels (LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, CRITICAL) were derived from gauge saturation rules (water_level >= danger_mark, rain > 200mm, discharge > 900k cusecs). Damage severity labels were official administrative classifications from post-disaster memorandums and mandal returns.

audit_finding: TARGET LEAKAGE DETECTED IN FLOOD MODEL
details: In Flood Risk, 'danger_ratio' (= water_level_m / danger_level_m) directly defines the CRITICAL threshold used to generate target labels, causing deterministic label leakage. This explains the 100% test accuracy. In Damage model, 'evacuated_population' is a post-warning operational response rather than a pure pre-impact feature.

audit_finding: SPLIT LEAKAGE IN DISASTER EVENTS; CLEAN IN SENSORS
details: Isolation Forest used a rigorous chronological split (80/20) without shuffle leakage. Flood and Damage models used random stratified splits across 22 rows; because multiple mandals belong to the same cyclone event, spatial/event autocorrelation leaked event baselines across train and test sets. Requires GroupKFold by cyclone_id for true out-of-event testing.

audit_finding: CLASS IMBALANCE IN DAMAGE; BALANCED IN INCIDENTS
details: Damage model has severe class imbalance: 'CATASTROPHIC' has only 2 samples (9%), while 'HIGH' has 9 samples (41%). In 75/25 split, test set has only 1 catastrophic sample. Flood model is balanced (5-6 per class). Incident corpus is exactly balanced in training (5 per class), but test set has only 1-2 per class.

audit_finding: NO GROUND TRUTH LABELS; HEURISTIC METRICS REPORTED
details: Isolation Forest is unsupervised. The training script reported 90.7% accuracy, which is merely the empirical inlier rate (1 - contamination), and precision/recall/F1 were fixed placeholder constants (0.95) rather than true confusion matrix metrics. Model functionally identifies deep pressure anomalies (-0.007 for 965 hPa), but metric claims must be labeled unsupervised inlier rate.

audit_finding: METRICS MATHEMATICALLY CORRECT BUT SMALL-SAMPLE VOLATILE
details: Scikit-learn accuracy, weighted precision, recall, and F1 calculations are mathematically correct. However, small test sets (N=6 for Flood, N=6 for Damage, N=8 for Incident) mean a single misclassification swings accuracy by 12.5% to 16.7%. Damage RF (Train 100%, Test 50%) and Incident LR (Train 100%, Test 50%) exhibit severe 50% overfit gaps.

Feature importances align with disaster engineering physics: Flood model prioritized rainfall_mm (26.6%), wind_speed_kmh (25.7%), danger_ratio (15.0%), and river discharge (13.3%). Damage model prioritized wind_speed_kmh (29.7%) and flood_depth_m (19.5%). Coordinates have low weights, avoiding spatial memorization.

audit_finding: ALL TEST INPUTS STRICTLY WITHIN TRAINING BOUNDARIES
details: Audited all test points in predict.py against training min/max envelopes: Flood example (rain 255mm, level 15.2m, flow 1.02M) is within [10-383mm, 9.2-104m, 15k-2.85M]. Damage example (wind 135 km/h, rain 245mm, depth 1.8m, pop 60k) is within [60-185, 95-383, 0.3-2.5, 22k-850k]. Sensor readings (45 km/h, 1005 hPa vs 155 km/h, 965 hPa) are within NOAA meteorological bounds.

All 4 model families (Random Forest, XGBoost, Isolation Forest, Logistic Regression) along with Scalers, LabelEncoders, and TfidfVectorizers load cleanly into memory via SahayaDisasterPredictor. Inference returns typed JSON/dictionaries with class probabilities, directly pluggable into FastAPI endpoints.
